title: Every tile honours the four-state contract with distinct visuals, role region, aria-live polite and non-colour distinction
asA: screen-reader user and colour-blind reader on the shipped dashboard
iWant: every tile state (loading, empty, error, populated) to carry a distinct visual, a labelled region, an aria-live polite announcer and a non-colour distinction
soThat: the tile's current state is reachable regardless of assistive tech and legible regardless of colour perception

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered tile in each of the four states (loading, empty, error, populated), the tile wraps its content in a `role="region"` element carrying `aria-live="polite"` and a labelled state descriptor (`data-tile-state="<state>"`). The state's visual cue is not colour-only: loading carries a skeleton stripe or spinner element, empty carries a labelled empty-state block, error carries a labelled error block with the recorded reason, populated carries the metric value. Every state exposes its accessible name as `<tile title>, <state>` on the wrapping region. Probed by the application-dashboard pack check AC-19103-1 (Playwright drives to `?tile=<id>&state=<state>` for each of the four states on each of two tiles, reads the accessibility tree and the DOM, and asserts every state carries the role region, the aria-live polite, the data-tile-state attribute, and a non-colour visual cue).
acceptanceCriteria.given: a tile switched into each of the four states
acceptanceCriteria.when: the DOM and the accessibility tree are read
acceptanceCriteria.then: each state carries role region, aria-live polite, data-tile-state, a non-colour visual cue and the announced name

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a tile transitioning between states (loading to populated, populated to error) at runtime, the tile's `aria-live="polite"` region announces the new state's accessible name to the assistive tech; the announcement text reads `<tile title>, <new state>` and the visual cue changes in the same paint. This AC is a runtime-observable behaviour on state transition; the pack does not simulate the transition today (the runner has no synthetic-event seam beyond click/type/press), so the AC is proven at project-side review and the README names the transition-observation gap under known mechanism-reach gaps.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the aria-live polite region announces the new state's accessible name and the visual cue changes

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered tile whose state is conveyed only through colour (a red border for error, a grey wash for loading, no text label or role), the pack fails the check per WCAG 1.4.1; a passing tile combines a non-colour visual cue (a shape, a text label, a spinner motion) and the accessible name reads `<tile title>, <state>`.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered tile whose state distinction is colour-only
acceptanceCriteria.when: the pack inspects the tile's visual and accessible name
acceptanceCriteria.then: the check fails; a passing tile combines a non-colour visual cue with a labelled state announcement

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered tile in the `error` state, the tile carries the recorded reason (an error record's `code` or a short message) visible in the DOM within the tile's region; a tile in the error state with no visible reason (an empty error block, an icon-only error indicator) fails the check.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered tile in the error state
acceptanceCriteria.when: the pack inspects the tile's region content
acceptanceCriteria.then: the tile carries a visible reason (error code or short message); an empty or icon-only error tile fails

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a tile transitioning rapidly across states (loading -> error -> loading -> populated within a 250ms window during a retry loop), the aria-live polite announcer coalesces or throttles announcements so assistive tech does not read four transitions in that window; the pack drives the fixture that fires the transitions and inspects the announcer's queued text at settle.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a tile transitioning across four states within a 250ms window
acceptanceCriteria.when: the aria-live polite announcer queues the transition text
acceptanceCriteria.then: announcements are coalesced or throttled so the reader hears the settled state, not every intermediate flip
